title: Cohomological delta-functors, their morphisms, and universal delta-functors
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. A *(cohomological) $\delta$-functor* $F=(F^n,\delta_F)$ from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ consists of (a) additive functors [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] $F^n:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $n\ge0$, and (b) for every short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$ (the morphisms $f,g$ being part of the data), morphisms $\delta_{F,A\to B\to C}^n:F^n(C)\to F^{n+1}(A)$ of $\mathcal B$, $n\ge0$, such that (1) for every short exact sequence the sequence $0\to F^0(A)\xrightarrow{F^0(f)}F^0(B)\xrightarrow{F^0(g)}F^0(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}F^1(A)\xrightarrow{F^1(f)}F^1(B)\xrightarrow{F^1(g)}F^1(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}F^2(A)\to\cdots$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], and (2) for every morphism $(a,b,c)$ of short exact sequences from $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ to $0\to A'\xrightarrow{f'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ (morphisms $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, $c:C\to C'$ with $b\circ f=f'\circ a$ and $c\circ g=g'\circ b$) one has $F^{n+1}(a)\circ\delta^n_{F,A\to B\to C}=\delta^n_{F,A'\to B'\to C'}\circ F^n(c)$ for all $n\ge0$. A *morphism of $\delta$-functors* $F\to G$ between $\delta$-functors $F=(F^n,\delta_F)$, $G=(G^n,\delta_G)$ from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ is a family of natural transformations $t^n:F^n\to G^n$, $n\ge0$, such that $t^{n+1}_A\circ\delta^n_{F,A\to B\to C}=\delta^n_{G,A\to B\to C}\circ t^n_C$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$ and every $n\ge0$. A $\delta$-functor $F$ is *universal* if for every $\delta$-functor $G$ from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ and every natural transformation $t:F^0\to G^0$ there is a unique morphism of $\delta$-functors $(t^n)_{n\ge0}:F\to G$ with $t^0=t$.

proof.text: *Remark: the $\delta$-functor clauses agree with Stacks' Definition 010Q.* Data (a) is 010Q data (1): a collection $F^n:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $n\ge0$, of *additive* functors (Stacks does require additivity, in the sense of 00ZY, which is [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]). Data (b) is 010Q data (2): for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$ (Stacks 010E: an exact complex, [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]) a collection $\delta_{A\to B\to C}:F^n(C)\to F^{n+1}(A)$, $n\ge0$; Stacks writes $\delta$ without the index $n$, the node writes $\delta^n$; Stacks indexes $\delta$ by the sequence $A\to B\to C$, i.e. by its morphisms, and the node says so explicitly. Axiom (1) is 010Q axiom (1): the displayed long sequence with unlabelled horizontal arrows, which are $F^n(f)$, $F^n(g)$, and diagonal arrows $\delta_{A\to B\to C}$, is exact; 'exact' for this one-sided infinite sequence is the variant of 010E for $x_1\to x_2\to\cdots$, i.e. a complex exact at every object after the initial $0$, which is how [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] reads; exactness at $F^0(A)$ says $F^0(f)$ is a monomorphism. Axiom (2) is 010Q axiom (2): for every morphism $(A\to B\to C)\to(A'\to B'\to C')$ of short exact sequences the square with horizontal arrows $\delta_{A\to B\to C}$, $\delta_{A'\to B'\to C'}$ and vertical arrows $F^n(C)\to F^n(C')$, $F^{n+1}(A)\to F^{n+1}(A')$ commutes. Stacks does not define 'morphism of short exact sequences' in Section 010P; it is a commutative diagram, i.e. a triple $(a,b,c)$ with $bf=f'a$, $cg=g'b$, and the vertical arrows of the square are $F^n(c)$ and $F^{n+1}(a)$; the node now writes the two commutation conditions out. No discrepancy: the earlier text already had additivity, $n\ge0$, the exact long sequence and the naturality square; only the two commutation conditions and the dependence of $\delta$ on $f,g$ were made explicit, and the maps $F^1(g)$, $\delta^1$ were added to the displayed sequence.

proof.text: *Remark: morphisms and universality agree with Stacks' Definitions 010R and 010S.* 010R: for $\delta$-functors $(F^n,\delta_F)$, $(G^n,\delta_G)$ from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$, a morphism is a collection of transformations of functors (natural transformations) $t^n:F^n\to G^n$, $n\ge0$, such that for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ the square $F^n(C)\xrightarrow{\delta_F}F^{n+1}(A)$, $G^n(C)\xrightarrow{\delta_G}G^{n+1}(A)$ with vertical arrows $t^n$ (at $C$) and $t^{n+1}$ (at $A$) commutes: this is the node's $t^{n+1}_A\circ\delta^n_{F,A\to B\to C}=\delta^n_{G,A\to B\to C}\circ t^n_C$. 010S: $F$ is universal iff for every $\delta$-functor $G$ and every morphism of functors $t:F^0\to G^0$ there is a unique morphism of $\delta$-functors $\{t^n\}_{n\ge0}:F\to G$ with $t=t^0$: the node's last sentence, word for word. Natural transformations are those of Mathlib (`CategoryTheory.NatTrans`); no node is needed for them.

*Remark: no claim is hidden in the definition.* The node only names data and conditions on them; it asserts no property. In particular it does not assert (i) the remark after 010Q that $F^0$ is left exact (a consequence of axiom (1): exactness of $0\to F^0(A)\to F^0(B)\to F^0(C)$), (ii) that $\delta$-functors with their morphisms form a category (identity $t^n=\mathrm{id}$; composite $(s^n\circ t^n)$, whose squares commute by pasting the two squares), or (iii) Lemma 010U, uniqueness of a universal $\delta$-functor with given $F^0$ up to unique isomorphism, which is a lemma, not part of 010S. Neither user of the node, [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal] (Stacks 010T) and [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], cites (i)-(iii) through this node; a later user that needs 010U must cite a statement node for it.
